wp-2ec7ab8ace9f32514114.title: 1961 Physics Nobel: follow the work, not just the award
wp-2ec7ab8ace9f32514114.summary: The source lists two laureates under one recognition year. Their work needs separate research records; a ceremony is a third kind of occurrence.

findings.text: Hofstadter's group published a Stanford electron-scattering experiment on 15 November 1953. That dates a publication, not the exact moment of discovery.
findings.sourceTitle: Original 1953 paper: Hofstadter, Fechter and McIntyre

findings.text: Stanford's institutional account identifies the Mark III accelerator and High Energy Physics Laboratory as the setting for Hofstadter's research.
TUM places Mössbauer's thesis research and the 1957 finding at the Max Planck institute in Heidelberg. His contribution should not inherit Hofstadter's Stanford location.
Stockholm's presentation ceremony belongs at the concert hall. Its recurring 10 December date is a recognition event; the Peace Prize has a separate Oslo venue history.

unresolved: Determine which particular experiment, result or publication should represent each research thread; preserve a period where no exact breakthrough day is documented.
Verify historical laboratory/venue coordinates rather than substituting modern campus, city-centre or award-time affiliation coordinates.
Keep ceremony, announcement, publication and discovery distinct. The original annual listing does not itself resolve those dates.
